threads.thread_goal: Align on current changeover steps and pick the pilot line scope.

messages.text:
Kicking off the changeover work for project_pack_ref: Standardise Assembly Line Changeover and Ergonomic Routines.
For task T1 we need to map how we actually do changeovers today on one line before we tidy anything up.
Can you all describe, in order, what you do from the moment the supervisor calls a product change until the first good part of the new product comes off the line? Rough steps and rough times are fine for now.
Also, we need to agree which line and shift we use as the pilot, so please share which line you know best and any issues you see there.

On Line 3 late shift, when they call a change we usually:
1) Stop the belt and clear the last parts into the finished bin.
2) Move leftover components from the station into the right totes, sometimes we just push them aside if we are in a hurry.
3) Swap the fixtures on the torque station, that takes about 5 to 7 minutes if nothing is stuck.
4) Adjust the height of the benches and the light arms.
5) Do a quick clean of the worktop and floor around the station.
6) Maintenance or the lead does a first piece check.
From call to first good part is around 25 to 30 minutes if all goes well.

On Line 2 early shift it is similar but we do some things in a different order:
1) Clear the belt and put a tag on any half-finished parts.
2) Wipe down the benches and change the small tools tray.
3) Change the bins for screws and small parts.
4) Adjust the stands and chairs.
5) Wait for the supervisor to bring the new paperwork.
I am not sure on the exact minutes, maybe around half an hour total, but I can try to time it next change if that helps.

On Line 1 night shift we:
1) Stop the line and press the reset.
2) Put the old labels away and get the new labels.
3) Change the boxes at the end of the line.
4) Clean the table and sweep a bit.
5) Wait for the ok from quality.
I do not know the times exactly, maybe 20 minutes, but sometimes longer when we cannot find the right labels.

Thanks, this is helpful. For T1 we need enough detail to see where we lose time and where we might be taking risks.
I suggest we capture:
- Main steps like you listed.
- Rough time per step, even if it is just 5, 10, 15 minutes.
- Any shortcuts we see, like pushing parts aside instead of putting them back properly.
Does that feel like the right level, or do we need more detail, like who does each step?

I think listing who usually does each step would help, because sometimes we wait for the lead or maintenance when we could start some parts ourselves.
Maybe we do not need every tiny move, but we should note when we are waiting on someone else or on paperwork.
I can try to write down who does what on Line 2 next time. I might miss some bits, so I will keep it simple and then you can tell me what is missing.
For me it is easier if we keep it to main steps and who is involved. If we go too detailed I will probably forget things when I am on the floor.

Ok, so for T1 let us agree we capture:
- Main steps in order.
- Rough time per step.
- Who usually does it.
- Any waiting time or shortcuts.
That should be enough detail without making it too heavy. I will log that in A8 so we keep it consistent.

From the time records side, it would help if we know the usual total changeover time per line and shift. That will feed into T8 and later T12.
So when you time the steps for T1, please also note the total duration from stop to first good part. I will use that later when we build the weekly summary in A6.
Got it, I will time the next changeover on Line 3 late shift and write down the total and the main steps like we said.

On picking the pilot line: my view is Line 3 late shift is a good candidate.
Reasons:
- We already have a rough list of steps from you.
- We see more small incidents there when people rush the clean up.
- The team is stable, so easier to test new routines.
Any strong reasons to pick Line 1 or Line 2 instead?
I am ok with Line 3 late shift as pilot. Line 2 early shift has more new starters right now, so maybe better to bring them in once things are clearer.
Fine by me too. Night shift on Line 1 is a bit stretched, so testing later there would be easier once we have posters and checklists ready.
I am happy to use Line 3 late shift as pilot. I can help collect the steps and any issues we see in the first runs and add them into A8.

Great, then we will lock in Line 3 late shift as the pilot scope for T1 and the next tasks.
I will note that in A8 so it is clear for the supervisor and safety officer.

To close this thread for now:
- We agreed the detail for T1 is main steps, rough time, who does it, and any waiting or shortcuts.
- We picked Line 3 late shift as the pilot line and shift.
Next step is to time at least two real changeovers on that line and write them up so we can move into drafting the new SOP in T2.

next_steps.when: next two changeovers on Line 3 late shift

threads.thread_goal: Draft and refine the new changeover SOP and visual guides.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the changeover steps for Line 3 late shift based on what we mapped in T1 and logged in A8.
The draft SOP is in A1 as Pilot Line Changeover SOP v1.
Can you read through and comment on:
- Any missing steps.
- Any steps that are in the wrong order.
- Anything that feels unsafe or hard to follow.
We also need to think which key steps should go onto the wall posters for T5 and A4, so please flag what you think must be visible at a glance on the floor.

I went through A1. Overall it matches what we do, but I see two gaps:
- After clearing the belt, we often forget to lock out the torque tool before changing the fixture. That should be a clear step.
- There is no step about checking the floor for oil or parts before we restart.
I would also move the paperwork check earlier, so we do not stand waiting at the end.

I read A1 too. Some of the sentences are a bit long for me.
For example, the step about cleaning and checking tools could maybe be split into two shorter steps.
For the posters in A4, I think we should only show:
- Stop and clear line.
- Lock out tools.
- Change fixtures and bins.
- Clean and check floor.
- First piece check.
The rest can stay in the full SOP.

I like the pictures idea for T5. On nights it is easier to follow a simple picture than a long text.
In A1 there is a step about adjusting lights and benches. Could we add a short note to remind people to set them to a comfortable height, not just copy the last person? That might help with backs and shoulders.

From my side, A1 looks fine in terms of steps that might affect time coding later.
One suggestion: could we number the main steps clearly, maybe 1 to 8, so that when we do the weekly summary in A6 we can say where delays happened? That will make T8 easier later.

Good catches.
I will update A1 to:
- Add a clear lock out step before fixture change.
- Add a floor and area check before restart.
- Move the paperwork check earlier, right after we stop and clear the line.
I will also split the long cleaning and tool check step as suggested and number the main steps for easier tracking.

On the posters for T5 and A4, I agree we keep only the key safety and sequence points.
Proposal for what goes on A4:
1) Stop line and clear parts.
2) Lock out tools.
3) Change fixtures and bins.
4) Adjust bench and lights to your body.
5) Clean area and check floor.
6) First piece check before restart.
Everything else stays in the full SOP A1.
If that sounds right, I will start sketching simple photo based guides.
That list for A4 works for me. Maybe we can add a small icon next to lock out tools and first piece check so they stand out more.

Yes, that is the right amount for the posters. If we add more, people will stop reading them.
For A1, can we also use simple words like start, stop, clean, check, instead of long phrases? That will help everyone on the floor.

Agreed. I will go through A1 and simplify the wording, keeping each step short and clear.
Once I have updated the draft, I will share back here for a quick final check before we call it the first pilot version for T2.

Update: I have now:
- Added lock out and floor check steps.
- Moved paperwork earlier.
- Numbered the main steps.
- Split long sentences and used simpler words.
Please have a quick second look at A1 and react here if you see any blockers for using this in the pilot.

I checked the new A1. The order looks right now and the extra safety checks are clear.
From my side we can use this version on Line 3 late shift for the pilot.

I read it again too. The shorter steps are easier to follow now.
I am ok to go ahead with this version for the pilot.

Looks good to me as well. The reminder about adjusting bench and lights is clear.
No issues from night shift side.

Thanks all. Based on your feedback, we will treat the current A1 as the approved first pilot version for T2.
For the posters in A4 under T5, we agreed they will show only the six key steps we listed, with simple icons for lock out and first piece check.
I will move ahead with preparing the visual drafts.

threads.thread_goal: Define ergonomic checklist and rotation schedule for the pilot.

messages.text:
Switching to ergonomics for the pilot.
I drafted some first items for the ergonomic workstation checklist in T3 and put them into A2.
Examples:
- Check bench height so forearms are roughly level.
- Place heavy parts close to the body.
- Keep tools within easy reach.
- Clear floor of trip hazards.
For rotation, I sketched a simple pattern in A3 for T4 where people move between three key stations on Line 3 late shift every 2 hours.
Can you review and say:
- What ergonomic checks we should add or remove.
- Whether the 2 hour rotation between the three stations feels workable with our current breaks.

In A2 I like the simple checks. Maybe we can add one about changing position, like do not stand still too long, and one about stretching hands before starting.
On the 2 hour rotation in A3, I am a bit worried it might clash with the main break. Maybe we can line up one of the moves with the break so it is easier to remember.

For A2 I would also add:
- Check that you can see the parts clearly without bending your neck too much.
- Make sure you can lift heavier items with both hands, not twisted.
We should keep the checklist short enough to do in under 5 minutes at shift start, so maybe no more than 8 items total.
On rotation in A3, 2 hours feels ok to me if we align one move with the main break like mentioned.

I sometimes forget to adjust the chair when I swap stations.
Could we add a checklist item in A2 about checking chair height and back support?
For rotation, I am ok with 2 hours, but I need a clear simple table that shows who is where at what time, otherwise I will get lost.

Good points.
For A2 under T3, I suggest we lock the checklist to 8 items:
1) Bench height.
2) Chair height and back support.
3) Tool reach.
4) Heavy parts close to body.
5) Clear floor.
6) Neck and view of parts.
7) Short hand and shoulder stretch.
8) Reminder to change position during the shift.
This should still be doable in under 5 minutes.
On A3 for T4, I will rework the rotation so one move lines up with the main break and put it into a simple table.

That list of 8 items in A2 sounds right to me. It is short enough that I can remember it.
For the rotation table in A3, can we also mark which station is heavier work and which is lighter, so we do not put people on heavy work back to back?

Yes, marking heavy and lighter stations in A3 is a good idea.
Maybe we can set the pattern so each person does one heavier, then one lighter, then a medium station in each shift. That should help with strain.

Ok, I will:
- Finalise A2 with the 8 checklist items we listed.
- Update A3 so the rotation pattern is heavy, light, medium for each person, with one move aligned to the main break.
Once updated, we should test the checklist on the floor to see if it really takes under 5 minutes and if the rotation fits the actual shift times.
Once you update A2 and A3, I can try the checklist at the start of my next shift and time it, and we can walk through the rotation pattern with the team to see if anyone spots issues.

I would like the checklist printed big near the line so I can follow it step by step.
The heavy, light, medium idea in A3 sounds good. I just need the table to be very clear, maybe with colours or simple labels.

I have now updated A2 and A3 with the agreed items and rotation pattern.
Before we lock them for the pilot, any last changes you want to see on the checklist items or the stations included in the rotation?

No more changes from me. The 8 items in A2 cover the main things I struggle with.
The three stations in A3 are the right ones to rotate between for strain.

Same here, I am happy with the checklist and the rotation pattern as they are now.
Let us use these for the pilot on Line 3 late shift.
Ok for me too. I will need a quick walk through on the floor, but the documents A2 and A3 look clear enough.

Great, then we will lock the ergonomic checklist in A2 for T3 and the rotation pattern in A3 for T4 as the pilot setup for Line 3 late shift.
We will still adjust after the first weeks if needed, but this will be our starting point.

threads.thread_goal: Clarify time coding, payroll impact, and weekly reporting.

messages.text:
I want to clarify how the new changeover and rotation routines will show up in time records for project_pack_ref: Standardise Assembly Line Changeover and Ergonomic Routines.
For T7 and T12 we need clear rules in A7 so that:
- Changeover time is coded consistently across shifts.
- Rotation time does not create confusion with breaks or downtime.
Also, for T8 we have the weekly summary template in A6, which needs inputs from the line.
Can you share how you currently record changeover time on Line 3 late shift, and whether you see any issues if we start coding it as a separate activity?

Right now on Line 3 late shift we just see changeover as part of normal working time. We do not press any special code on the terminal, we just stop the line and then start again.
If we add a separate code, we will need a simple rule on when to start and stop it, otherwise people will forget.

On Line 2 early shift it is the same, no special code.
I am ok to use a new code if it is just one button and the supervisor reminds us at the start.

Thanks, that helps.
My proposal for A7 under T7 is:
- Use one code for changeover time, started when the supervisor calls the change and the line stops, and ended when the first good part of the new product is confirmed.
- Rotation between stations during normal running stays under normal working time, no extra code.
This keeps it simple and matches how we measure changeover in A6 for T8.
Any concerns with that start and end rule?

That rule sounds clear to me.
We just need to make sure the supervisor is the one who starts and stops the code, so operators can focus on the steps in A1 and the checklist in A2.
For rotation, I agree it should stay as normal time, otherwise it will get messy.

If the supervisor handles the code, I am fine with that rule.
We just need a short note for the team so everyone knows that changeover is now tracked separately but does not change their pay in a strange way.
I am ok with one simple code. Please keep the explanation short and clear, maybe with an example of a payslip so we can see nothing odd happens.

Good point.
For T12 I will prepare a short note in A7 explaining:
- Changeover time is now coded separately with the new code.
- It still counts as normal working time for pay.
- It helps us see how long changeovers take and where we improve.
I will also run a couple of sample payslips under T12 to check there are no unexpected impacts.

On the weekly summary in A6 for T8, my idea is:
- Supervisor or lead on Line 3 late shift notes total changeover time and incident count from A5 and A1 for the week.
- They fill A6 once a week and send it to me.
- I check for any odd patterns and share back a short comment.
Is it realistic for the lead to fill A6 weekly, or do we need to simplify further?

I think the lead can handle filling A6 weekly if we keep it short.
Maybe we can pre fill some fields and only ask them to enter:
- Number of changeovers.
- Average time.
- Number of incidents or near misses from A5.
That should be manageable.

Agree, as long as the template in A6 is simple and we remind the lead at the end of the week, it should work.
We can also help by making sure A5 is filled in properly when something happens.

Ok, I will adjust A6 so the lead only needs to fill those three fields.
To summarise the rules for A7 under T7 and T12:
- One code for changeover, started at line stop for product change and ended at first good part.
- Supervisor or lead is responsible for starting and stopping the code.
- Rotation time stays as normal working time.
Unless there are objections, I will treat this as our agreed approach for the pilot.
No objections from me. That setup is clear and should not add extra work for operators.
Fine by me too. As long as the supervisor handles the code and we get the short note you mentioned, I am comfortable with this.

Great, then we will lock these time coding rules in A7 for T7 and T12.
For the weekly summary, we will use A6 with the simplified fields and the Line 3 late shift lead as the owner for T8.
I will document this and share the short note for workers before we start the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Run pilot check-in, review incidents and feedback, and decide updates.

messages.text:
End of first pilot week check in for Line 3 late shift.
For T6, T9, T10 and T11 we need to:
- Share any incidents or near misses logged in A5.
- Capture feedback from the training briefing and floor use in A8.
- Decide what to change in A1, A2, A3 and A4 before we extend further.
Please post:
- Any incidents or near misses during changeover or related to ergonomics.
- What worked well with the new SOP and checklist.
- What was confusing or slowed you down.

From this week on Line 3 late shift:
- We had one near miss where a part was left on the floor near the torque station. It was spotted before anyone tripped. I logged it in A5.
- The lock out step in A1 worked well, people followed it.
- The main slowdown was waiting for paperwork at the start of one changeover, about 5 minutes.
The ergonomic checklist in A2 took about 4 minutes to complete at shift start when I timed it.

I joined the briefing under T9 and then did one changeover with the new SOP.
What worked:
- The posters in A4 helped me remember the order.
- The reminder to adjust bench and lights made a difference for my shoulders.
What was confusing:
- I was not sure where to sign that I had done the ergonomic checklist in A2. Maybe we need a simple tick box sheet.

From night shift support on Line 3:
- No incidents, but one person said the poster A4 was a bit small to read from their station.
- The rotation pattern in A3 was ok, but we forgot one move until the supervisor reminded us.
- The checklist A2 was fine once someone read it out loud at the start.

From the time and log side:
- A5 shows one near miss as mentioned and no recordable incidents.
- A6 for this week shows average changeover time of 24 minutes, slightly better than the 25 to 30 minutes we had before.
- The new changeover code in A7 was used correctly on all three changeovers.
So from data, the pilot looks stable so far.

Thanks for the inputs.
From what I hear so far, possible adjustments:
- In A1, add a small note to double check the floor for loose parts right after clearing the line, to reduce the near miss risk.
- In A2, add a simple tick box sheet or space to sign off.
- In A3, maybe add a small reminder on the poster or at the board about the rotation move times.
Any other changes you think we should make now, or should we keep the rest as is for another week?

Those changes sound right to me.
I would also suggest in A1 we highlight the paperwork step a bit more, maybe with a note to prepare it before the planned changeover when possible, to avoid the 5 minute wait we had.

I agree with adding a tick box sheet for A2. If we keep it near the line, I can just tick my name at the start.
No other changes from me right now, I would like to run it one more week to see if anything else comes up.

Making the poster A4 a bit bigger or moving it closer would help.
For A3, a small note on the whiteboard with the rotation times would be enough for me.

Ok, so proposed updates for T11 are:
- A1: emphasise floor check and paperwork preparation.
- A2: add a simple tick box sheet for sign off.
- A3: add a reminder about rotation move times.
- A4: adjust size or placement so it is easier to read.
I will mark these changes clearly in the next version and log them in A8.
Do we all agree these are the right changes to implement now?

Yes, I agree with that list of changes.
Once you update A1 to A4, I can help check on the floor that the new versions are in the right places and the old ones are removed.
I am ok with those changes too. The tick box sheet will make it easier to remember the checklist.
Agreed. Please let us know when the new posters and sheets are up so we can start using them.

From the data side, these changes are small and should not affect the time coding rules in A7 or the weekly summary in A6.
I support implementing them now and then checking A5 and A6 again after the next two weeks.

Great, then we will go ahead and update A1 to A4 as described for T11.
I will version the documents, get them rechecked with the supervisor and safety officer, and make sure old versions are removed from the floor.
That covers which SOP and checklist changes we implement after this first pilot week.

On readiness to extend beyond Line 3 late shift:
- Incidents are low and logged in A5.
- Average changeover time improved slightly in A6.
- Feedback is mostly about small tweaks, not big problems.
My suggestion is:
- After we apply the T11 updates and run two more weeks on Line 3, we consider rolling out to Line 2 early shift next, using the same materials.
Do you feel we are on track for that, or should we wait longer before extending?

I think two more weeks on Line 3 with the updated documents is enough before we move to Line 2.
By then we will know if the new floor check and paperwork notes in A1 really help.

From Line 2 side, I would be ready to try the new SOP and checklist after those two extra weeks.
It will help if we get the same kind of short briefing as you did for T9 on Line 3.
I agree with that plan. Night shift will also benefit from the improved posters and checklist once they are updated.

From my side, as long as we keep using A7 and A6 the same way, extending to Line 2 after two more weeks on Line 3 is fine.
I will just need to check a couple of sample payslips again under T12 when we add the new line.

Ok, then we will treat the pilot as ready to extend after:
- Applying the T11 updates to A1 to A4.
- Running two more weeks on Line 3 and reviewing A5, A6 and A8 again.
If no major issues appear, we will start rollout to Line 2 early shift with the same SOP, checklist, rotation and posters.
I will note this plan in A8 so it is clear for the supervisor.
